answer: The jury's own reward depends on rejecting low-quality answers, creating a shared incentive among honest graders to spot coordinated fakery, so a Sybil cluster collapses under the weight of its own low scores. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds.. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. Consider a kernel as the anchor of the cost. A sable stands in for the reward an honest agent protects...
